title: Fed rate hike announcement on bank stock returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Classic event–study design.  
Why: We have a single, well-defined, exogenous shock (an unanticipated Fed rate-hike announcement) that hits all treated firms (banks) on the same event date. With pre-event estimation data we can build a counterfactual return series and recover abnormal returns.  
Key identifying assumptions  
• Market–model validity: E[ε_it | R_mkt,t]=0 so expected return = α_i + β_i R_mkt,t.  
• No confounding firm–specific or market-wide news in the (−1,+1) window.  
• Abnormal returns are i.i.d. across firms, so cross-sectional t-tests are valid.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
library(data.table)  # fast aggregation
library(broom)       # tidy regression output

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s11_data.csv"
dt   <- fread(path)

# 2. Baseline abnormal returns using provided beta -------------------------
dt[, exp_ret_beta := beta * mkt_ret]                 # assume alpha = 0
dt[, ar_beta      := ret - exp_ret_beta]             # abnormal return

# 3. Event-window CAR [-1,+1] ----------------------------------------------
event_window <- -1:1
car_beta <- dt[event_day %in% event_window,
               .(CAR = sum(ar_beta)),
               by = stock_id]

# Cross-sectional statistics
N  <- nrow(car_beta)
mu <- mean(car_beta$CAR)
se <- sd(car_beta$CAR)/sqrt(N)
t_stat <- mu / se

cat("======== Baseline (provided beta, alpha = 0) ========\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean CAR  [-1,+1]  : %0.4f\n", mu))
cat(sprintf("Std. Error        : %0.4f\n", se))
cat(sprintf("t-stat (H0: CAR=0): %0.2f\n\n", t_stat))

# 4. Robustness check 1: re-estimate alpha & beta in estimation window ------
est_dt <- dt[event_day %between% c(-10,-2)]

# run firm-level regressions
estimates <- est_dt[, {
  fit <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)
  tidy(fit)[1:2,2]          # alpha & beta estimates
}, by = stock_id]

setnames(estimates, c("term","estimate"), c("param","value"))
estimates <- dcast(estimates, stock_id ~ param, value.var = "value")

# merge back
dt2 <- merge(dt, estimates, by = "stock_id")
dt2[, exp_ret_ols := `(Intercept)` + mkt_ret * mkt_ret.1]  # mistake? Wait: we need names.
```

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model; estimation window [−10,−2]; event window [−1,+1]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank stocks show negative CAR around the rate hike announcement
